en: Section B Interview.
zh: B节：访谈。

en: In this section you will hear one interview.
zh: 在这一节中，你将听到一段访谈。

en: The interview will be divided into two parts.
zh: 这段访谈分为两部分。

en: At the end of each part, five questions will be asked about what was said.
zh: 每部分结束后，将就刚才所说的内容提出五个问题。

en: Both the interview and the questions will be spoken once only.
zh: 访谈和问题都只读一遍。

en: After each question, there will be a ten-second pause.
zh: 每个问题之后会有十秒钟的停顿。

en: During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C, and D, and mark the best answer to each question on Answer Sheet II.
zh: 请利用停顿时间阅读A、B、C、D四个选项，并在答题卡二上标出每题的最佳答案。

en: You have thirty seconds to preview the questions.
zh: 你有三十秒钟预览题目。

en: Now listen to part one of the interview.
zh: 现在请听访谈的第一部分。

en: Questions one to five are based on part one of the interview.
zh: 第1至5题根据访谈的第一部分提问。

en: The word diversity has become a cliché in the United States today.
zh: 如今在美国，“多样性”这个词已成了老生常谈。

en: It seems to me that nowadays Americans cannot turn on the television or read a newspaper
zh: 在我看来，如今美国人只要打开电视或翻开报纸，

en: without seeing the word pop up somewhere as a description of the American demographic.
zh: 就会在某处看到这个词，用来描述美国的人口构成。

en: Then what is this diversity in the US?
zh: 那么，美国所说的这种多样性到底是什么呢？

en: Today, we are very pleased to have Dr James Johnson here on our talk show.
zh: 今天，我们很高兴邀请到詹姆斯·约翰逊博士做客访谈节目。

en: Welcome, Dr Johnson.
zh: 欢迎您，约翰逊博士。

en: Thanks.
zh: 谢谢。

en: Dr Johnson, we know you have done extensive research on diversity.
zh: 约翰逊博士，我们知道，您对多样性做过广泛的研究。

en: So, what is, how do you define diversity in the American context?
zh: 那么，什么是……您如何定义美国社会语境中的多样性？

en: Well, at one time the US was called a melting pot, you know, which means that people of many different religions, cultures, and races
zh: 嗯，美国曾被称为“大熔炉”，也就是说，信仰、文化和种族各不相同的人，

en: could shed their traditional cultural identities and blend into one homogeneous nation.
zh: 可以放下原有的传统文化身份，融合为一个同质的国家。

en: Am I right in saying that a melting pot would emphasize the idea of all in one or being the same?
zh: 我可以这样理解吗：大熔炉强调的是融为一体，或者变得相同？

en: Yes, you may say so.
zh: 是的，可以这么说。

en: Um, of course, when the phrase “melting pot” was popular, there was also the idea of being different,
zh: 嗯，当然，在“大熔炉”这个说法流行时，也存在差异的观念，

en: but being different then simply meant Catholic as opposed to Protestant, or Irish as opposed to Swedish or Italian.
zh: 不过那时所谓的不同，只是天主教徒相对于新教徒，或者爱尔兰裔相对于瑞典裔、意大利裔的差别。

en: Has the idea of being different changed over the years?
zh: 这些年来，人们对于“不同”的理解发生变化了吗？

en: Yes, of course.
zh: 是的，当然发生了变化。

en: You see today, we use the word diversity to refer to more-visible ethnic differences —
zh: 你看，如今我们用“多样性”指更为明显的族裔差异，

en: Asian American, African American, and Latino, for instance.
zh: 例如亚裔美国人、非裔美国人以及拉丁裔。

en: And religious diversity refers to a variety of world religions, not merely different branches of Christianity.
zh: 宗教多样性指的是世界上的各种宗教，而不仅仅是基督教内部的不同教派。

en: And now is America as a whole truly diverse?
zh: 那么，如今美国整体上真的具有多样性吗？

en: Well, I think in all this talk of diversity there is a critical point that may be missed: that is,
zh: 嗯，我认为，在所有这些关于多样性的讨论中，人们可能忽略了一个关键点：

en: diversity is not occurring everywhere in the US, or at least not to a degree that would alter the demography of every region in the country.
zh: 多样化并未发生在美国所有地方，至少还没有达到改变全国每个地区人口构成的程度。

en: Oh, really?
zh: 哦，是这样吗？

en: I can give you an example.
zh: 我可以举个例子。

en: Recently a New York Times article describes the town of Selinsgrove in Pennsylvania.
zh: 最近，《纽约时报》的一篇文章介绍了宾夕法尼亚州的塞林斯格罗夫镇。

en: You see, in the last 10 years things have barely changed in that town.
zh: 你看，过去十年里，那个小镇几乎没有变化。

en: The population has dropped by one, from 5,384 to 5,383 and the town remains virtually 100% white.
zh: 人口只减少了一人，从5384人降到5383人，而镇上的居民仍然几乎百分之百是白人。

en: The article thus concludes that many portions of the country remain, like Selinsgrove, virtually unchanged on this march towards “diversity.”
zh: 因此，这篇文章得出结论：在迈向“多样性”的进程中，美国的许多地方仍像塞林斯格罗夫一样，几乎没有变化。

en: So regions vary in terms of the degree and types of diversity?
zh: 所以，各地区多样性的程度和类型有所不同，是吗？

en: That’s correct.
zh: 没错。

en: Let’s say there are 3 types of diversity in the US.
zh: 我们姑且说，美国存在三种多样性。

en: And they differ from region to region.
zh: 而且，它们因地区而异。

en: Could you elaborate on that?
zh: 您能详细说明一下吗？

en: OK. The first is racial diversity.
zh: 好的。第一种是种族多样性。

en: States with the most racially diverse populations stand in stark contrast to those with the least racially diverse populations.
zh: 人口种族构成最多样的州，与种族构成最单一的州形成了鲜明对比。

en: Um, let’s look at two states, California and Maine.
zh: 嗯，我们来看两个州：加利福尼亚州和缅因州。

en: From 1990 to 2000, California’s Caucasian population — meaning non-Hispanic whites — declined from 57% to 48%.
zh: 从1990年到2000年，加州的高加索裔人口，也就是非西班牙裔白人，占比从57%降到了48%。

en: By 2025, it is predicted, that figure will drop to just 34%, which indicates a future change in the racial composition of California.
zh: 据预测，到2025年，这一比例将降到仅34%，这反映出加州未来种族构成的变化。

en: On the contrary, Maine’s Caucasian population was 98% of its total population throughout the 1990s; and by 2025,
zh: 相反，整个20世纪90年代，缅因州的高加索裔人口占总人口的98%；到2025年，

en: Maine’s population will still be 97% Caucasian, which means virtually no change in Maine’s racial diversity over the next 20 or so years.
zh: 这个比例仍将为97%，也就是说，在之后二十年左右的时间里，缅因州的种族多样性几乎不会发生变化。

en: This is the end of part one of the interview.
zh: 访谈的第一部分到此结束。

en: Questions one to five are based on what you have just heard.
zh: 第1至5题根据你刚才听到的内容提问。

en: Question 1. Why does the woman say the word diversity has become a cliche?
zh: 为什么女士说“多样性”这个词已成为老生常谈？

en: Question 2. According to Dr Johnson, what is diversity in America?
zh: 根据约翰逊博士的说法，美国的多样性指什么？

en: Question 3. What does the example of Selinsgrove show?
zh: 塞林斯格罗夫的例子说明了什么？

en: Question 4. According to Dr Johnson, which place will witness a radical change in its racial makeup by 2025?
zh: 根据约翰逊博士的说法，到2025年，哪个地方的种族构成将发生巨大变化？

en: Question 5. What is the similarity between Selinsgrove and Maine according to the interview?
zh: 根据访谈，塞林斯格罗夫与缅因州有什么相似之处？
